verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents QoS settings for non-ideal networks and topics for streaming sensor data, and a long-time user says ROS provides teleop 'for free' if you follow its conventions. However, no first-party teleoperation feature is documented, and live video streaming and responsiveness over real-world remote networks are not evidenced; most of what exists is middleware building blocks. Missing for 10: documented teleop tooling, live video streaming/transport, remote/WAN connectivity guidance, latency or responsiveness evidence, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops lead, I can teleoperate a remote robot with live video and responsive control over real-world networks

citations.quote: Quality of service settings for handling non-ideal networks
The topic interface is meant for continuous data streams, for example, streaming sensor data or the status of your robot.
ROS gives you data bagging, visualization, teleop and sim 'for free' if you follow its conventions
